newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares soar as demand burgeons.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares soar as demand burgeons.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 3.4 percent on Thursday on spirited demand from both foreign and domestic investors and traders said the trend looked set to continue over the medium term.
"The demand is very strong. Foreign buying is particularly strong in Lek and Terme Catez," said Bogdan Pusnik, a trader at brokerage Medvesek Pusnik.

Shares have surged 22.5 percent since January 6 on hopes of strong business results from companies like drug maker Lek and health resort operator Terme Catez coupled with an end to the political vacuum.

Following the inconclusive November general election, parliament two weeks ago gave the mandate to form a new government to centre-left Liberal Democrat Janez Drnovsek, who must present his government lineup by Friday.
Issue A of Lek has risen 55.7 percent since the beginning of 1997, while Terme Catez has jumped 30.2 percent.
Traders said Wednesday's news that the Bank of Slovenia approved a London listing of the country's second largest bank SKB, pushed up shares of other listed banks, although SKB was not traded.
SKB shares were suspended from Tuesday as on Monday their average price rose by over 30 percent since the bank's last public announcement on the price of its shares.
Bourse regulations stipulate that trading be suspended after such a rise or fall until the company concerned issues a statement on why it believes the share price has made such a move.
Trading in SKB will resume a day after the bank issues a new statement to explain the share price movement. The bank said earlier it would issue the statement by Friday.
Probanka was up 8.97 percent, while the preferred shares of Dolenjska banka rose 8.11 percent.
The SBI index jumped 46.56 points to 1,415.4. Turnover rose to 459.2 million tolars from 386.6 million. 13 shares rose, three were unchanged, four fell and five were untraded.
Issue A of drug company Lek had the highest turnover, rising 5.12 percent to 30,400 tolars on volume of 9,545 shares for total turnover of 285.5 million tolars.
Ordinary shares of trader Kovinotehna were the top gainers, up 10 percent to 517 tolars on volume of 15,108 shares for total turnover of 7.6 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, closing 8.4 lower at 18,320 on volume of 92 shares for total turnover of 1.8 million tolars.
Health resort operator Terme Catez rose 7.98 percent to 14,200 on volume of 3,647 shares for total turnover of 50.5 million tolars.
